title: CHAPTER SEVEN. On the attributes of God; essential properties not accidents
latin: CAPUT SEPTIMUM, De attributis DEI. Adeo huc usque sunt nomina divina: Sequuntur attributa, quae sunt instar proprietatum, naturam Dei, ut ea pro captu nostro aliquo modo adumbrata fuit, quasi consequentium, quibus omnis perfectio essentiae Dei nobis plenius declaratur. Attributa in divinis primum invenisse usum, erudite docet diffusae eruditionis vir, DAN. HEINSIUS, Aristarchi sacri cap. 2., pag. 42. Vulgo dicuntur proprietates essentiales, naturalesve & perfectiones Dei, quae sane non sunt qualitates, quae essentiae Dei accident, sed ipsissima Dei essentia. Qua de causa neque distinguuntur a priori aut reipsa ab essentia aut inter se, sed formaliter, nostroque concipiendi modo, neque recipiunt magis & minus.
english: CHAPTER SEVEN. On the attributes of God.

Thus far have been the divine names: there follow the attributes, which are after the manner of properties almost consequent upon the nature of God as it was somehow sketched for our capacity, by which every perfection of God's essence is more fully declared to us.

That attributes first found use in divine matters, Daniel Heinsius, a man of wide learning, teaches learnedly (Aristarchus sacer, chapter 2, p. 42). They are commonly called essential or natural properties and perfections of God, which indeed are not qualities that happen upon God's essence, but God's very essence itself. For which reason they are not distinguished a priori or in the thing itself from the essence or among themselves, but formally and by our mode of conceiving, nor do they admit more and less.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER SEVEN. Concerning ye attributes belonging toward God. Thus far ye divine names have been: there follow ye attributes, which after ye manner belonging toward properties almost consequent upon ye nature belonging toward God as for our capacity somehow it was sketched stand, by which every perfection belonging toward God's essence more fully unto us is declared. That attributes first in divine matters found use, Daniel Heinsius, a man belonging toward wide learning, learnedly teaches (Aristarchus sacer, chapter 2, p. 42). Commonly essential or natural properties plus perfections belonging toward God they are called, which indeed are not qualities that upon God's essence happen, but God's very essence itself. For which reason a priori or in ye thing itself from ye essence or among themselves they are not distinguished, but formally plus by our mode belonging toward conceiving, nor more plus less do they admit.

title: II. Proper or figurative attributes; three genera of proper attributes
latin: II. Attributa Dei sunt propria aut figurata. Attributa Dei propria trium sunt generum. Alia sunt, ut entis, alia, ut viventis virtualiter, alia, ut viventis integre. Illa conveniunt Deo simpliciter, respectu essentiae, quatenus est summo modo: ista evidenter, respectu vitae intelligentis, quatenus intelligit, vult, agit & operatur: haec excellenter, respectu virtutis ac beatitudinis, quatenus bene beateque agit. Hoc probatur conjunctim ac discretim. Conjunctim, verbis VERI & VIVI, Jer. 10.10; 1 Thess. 1.9; Apoc. 1.17.18. Discretim, respectu essentiae, Exod. 3.14; Esai. 44.6; Apoc. 1.8 & 21.6 & 22.13; respectu vitae spiritualis, Deut. 32.40; Jud. 8.19; 1 Sam. 25.34; Psal. 18.47; 84.3; Joh. 4.24; 1 Tim. 1.17; Col. 1.15; respectu integritatis, Deut. 32.4; Matth. 5.48.
english: II. The attributes of God are proper or figurative. The proper attributes of God are of three genera. Some are as of being; others as of living virtually; others as of living integrally.

Those belong to God simply, with respect to essence, insofar as He is in the highest manner; these evidently, with respect to intelligent life, insofar as He understands, wills, acts, and works; these excellently, with respect to virtue and beatitude, insofar as He acts well and blessedly. This is proved jointly and separately. Jointly, by the words TRUE and LIVING (Jeremiah 10:10; 1 Thessalonians 1:9; Revelation 1:17-18). Separately, with respect to essence (Exodus 3:14; Isaiah 44:6; Revelation 1:8 and 21:6 and 22:13); with respect to spiritual life (Deuteronomy 32:40; Judges 8:19; 1 Samuel 25:34; Psalm 18:47; 84:3; John 4:24; 1 Timothy 1:17; Colossians 1:15); with respect to integrity (Deuteronomy 32:4; Matthew 5:48).
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): II. Ye attributes belonging toward God are proper or figurative. Ye proper attributes belonging toward God of three genera are. Some as of being are; others as of living virtually; others as of living integrally. Those unto God simply belong, with respect unto essence, insofar as in ye highest manner He is; these evidently, with respect unto intelligent life, insofar as He understands, wills, acts, plus works; these excellently, with respect unto virtue plus beatitude, insofar as well plus blessedly He acts. This jointly plus separately is proved. Jointly, by ye words TRUE plus LIVING (Jeremiah 10:10; 1 Thessalonians 1:9; Revelation 1:17-18). Separately, with respect unto essence (Exodus 3:14; Isaiah 44:6; Revelation 1:8 plus 21:6 plus 22:13); with respect unto spiritual life (Deuteronomy 32:40; Judges 8:19; 1 Samuel 25:34; Psalm 18:47; 84:3; John 4:24; 1 Timothy 1:17; Colossians 1:15); with respect unto integrity (Deuteronomy 32:4; Matthew 5:48).

title: III–IV. First-genus attributes by removal of creaturely imperfections; the six
latin: III. Primi generis attributa sunt, quae absolutam essentiae divinae perfectionem, per quam omnibus illa supereminet, remotione earum imperfectionum, quae communiter insunt creaturis, designant. Hacpropter, si modo accurate loquamur, creaturis nullo modo attribui possunt. IV. Sunt autem sex, nimirum 1. absoluta exsistendi necessitas, 2. infinitas, 3. simplicitas, 4. immutabilitas, 5. immensitas, 6. aeternitas. Ad haec caetera, quae ab aliis addi consueverunt, nullo negotio revocari queunt. His vero creaturarum proprietates opponuntur, quae quia significant imperfectionem, per quam illae a summa Dei perfectione deficiunt, a Deo removeri debent, ut sunt 1. contingentia, 2. finitudo, 3. multiplex compositio, 4. mutabilitas, 5. praesentia localis definita ad certum determinatumque spatium, 6. duratio finita. Haec autem, quae primi generis attributa diximus, omnia sunt negativa, quia per negationes a nobis concipiuntur & explicantur: iis tamen in Deo respondet positiva perfectio, quae istius negationis est fundamentum.
english: III. Attributes of the first genus are those which designate the absolute perfection of the divine essence, by which it stands above all, by the removal of those imperfections which commonly inhere in creatures. For this reason, if we speak accurately, they can in no way be attributed to creatures.

IV. But they are six, namely: 1. absolute necessity of existing; 2. infinity; 3. simplicity; 4. immutability; 5. immensity; 6. eternity. To these the rest which others have been accustomed to add can without difficulty be reduced. But to these the properties of creatures are opposed, which, because they signify imperfection by which those fall short of God's highest perfection, ought to be removed from God — as are 1. contingency; 2. finitude; 3. multiplex composition; 4. mutability; 5. local presence defined to a certain and determined space; 6. finite duration.

But these which we have called attributes of the first genus are all negative, because they are conceived and explained by us through negations: yet to them in God there answers a positive perfection which is the foundation of that negation.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): III. Attributes belonging toward ye first genus are those which ye absolute perfection belonging toward ye divine essence, by which above all it stands, by ye removal belonging toward those imperfections which commonly in creatures inhere, designate. For this reason, if accurately we speak, unto creatures in no way can they be attributed. IV. But six they are, namely: 1. absolute necessity belonging toward existing; 2. infinity; 3. simplicity; 4. immutability; 5. immensity; 6. eternity. Unto these ye rest which others to add have been accustomed without difficulty can be reduced. But unto these ye properties belonging toward creatures are opposed, which, because imperfection by which those from God's highest perfection fall short they signify, from God ought to be removed — as are 1. contingency; 2. finitude; 3. multiplex composition; 4. mutability; 5. local presence defined unto a certain plus determined space; 6. finite duration. But these which attributes belonging toward ye first genus we have called all negative are, because through negations by us they are conceived plus explained: yet unto them in God a positive perfection which ye foundation belonging toward that negation is answers.

title: V. General canons 1–6 on the divine attributes
latin: V. Sunt autem hic observandi generales CANONES. 1. Attributa Dei, sive proprietates ipsius essentiales, uno modo, quia infinitam essentiae divinae perfectionem uno conceptu totam comprehendere nequimus, sed aliquatenus duntaxat apprehendimus. 2. In attributis Dei non est prius & posterius nisi quantum ad nos. Quia enim omnia cum essentia unum sunt, in seipsis prius & posterius non admittunt. 3. Attributa Dei non recipiunt magis & minus in seipsis. At effecta eorum possunt admittere intensionem ac remissionem. 4. Attributa Dei non sunt sibi invicem contraria. At effecta eorum possunt esse contraria, ut sol una eademque virtute sua indurat lutum & liquefacit ceram. 5. Attributa DEI in se spectata sunt prorsus incommunicabilia. Sunt enim ipsissima Dei essentia. Neque tamen perperam distinguuntur in communicabilia & incommunicabilia, quia quaedam creaturis imprimunt sui imaginem, ut sapientia, bonitas, quaedam vix vestigium aut umbram tenuissimam. 6. Attributa Dei non multiplicantur in personis S. Trinitatis. Sicut enim una est essentia Patris, Filii & Spiritus sancti: sic quoque est una aeternitas, omnipotentia &c. Quapropter licet Pater sit omnipotens, & Filius omnipotens & Spiritus s. omnipotens: tamen non sunt tres omnipotentes, sed tres illi sunt unus omnipotens DEUS.
english: V. But here general CANONS are to be observed. 1. The attributes of God, or His essential properties, [are many] in one manner, because we cannot comprehend the whole infinite perfection of the divine essence in one concept, but only apprehend it to some extent.

2. In the attributes of God there is not prior and posterior except as regards us. For since all are one with the essence, in themselves they do not admit prior and posterior. 3. The attributes of God do not admit more and less in themselves. But their effects can admit intensification and remission. 4. The attributes of God are not contrary to one another. But their effects can be contrary, as the sun by one and the same virtue hardens mud and melts wax.

5. The attributes of GOD viewed in themselves are altogether incommunicable. For they are God's very essence itself. Yet they are not wrongly distinguished into communicable and incommunicable, because some impress their image on creatures, as wisdom and goodness, some scarcely a vestige or thinnest shadow. 6. The attributes of God are not multiplied in the persons of the Holy Trinity. For just as there is one essence of Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, so also there is one eternity, omnipotence, etc. Therefore although the Father is omnipotent, and the Son omnipotent, and the Holy Spirit omnipotent: yet there are not three omnipotent ones, but those three are one omnipotent GOD.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): V. But here general CANONS are to be observed. 1. Ye attributes belonging toward God, or His essential properties, [many] in one manner are, because ye whole infinite perfection belonging toward ye divine essence in one concept we cannot comprehend, but only to some extent apprehend. 2. In ye attributes belonging toward God prior plus posterior there is not except as regards us. For since all with ye essence one are, in themselves prior plus posterior they do not admit. 3. Ye attributes belonging toward God more plus less in themselves do not admit. But their effects intensification plus remission can admit. 4. Ye attributes belonging toward God unto one another contrary are not. But their effects contrary can be, as ye sun by one plus ye same virtue mud hardens plus wax melts. 5. Ye attributes belonging toward GOD in themselves viewed altogether incommunicable are. For God's very essence itself they are. Yet into communicable plus incommunicable not wrongly are they distinguished, because some their image upon creatures impress, as wisdom plus goodness, some scarcely a vestige or thinnest shadow. 6. Ye attributes belonging toward God in ye persons belonging toward ye Holy Trinity are not multiplied. For just as one essence belonging toward Father, Son, plus Holy Spirit there is, so also one eternity, omnipotence, etc. there is. Therefore although ye Father omnipotent is, plus ye Son omnipotent, plus ye Holy Spirit omnipotent: yet three omnipotent ones there are not, but those three one omnipotent GOD are.

title: Canon 7: attributes govern all theology — Cap. 7 close
latin: 7. Attributa DEI dividunt universam theologiam. Nam in omnibus commentationibus, disputationibus, concionibusque theologicis respiciendum est ad attributa Dei, ne quid statuatur iis contrarium. Et in universa Christiana vita pro cynosura sunt haec attributa, ut Deum revereamur & imitemur, solidumque percipiamus solatium.
english: 7. The attributes of GOD divide universal theology. For in all theological comments, disputations, and sermons regard is to be had to the attributes of God, lest anything contrary to them be established. And in the whole Christian life these attributes are as a cynosure, that we may revere and imitate God, and perceive solid consolation.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): 7. Ye attributes belonging toward GOD universal theology divide. For in all theological comments, disputations, plus sermons regard unto ye attributes belonging toward God is to be had, lest anything contrary unto them be established. And in ye whole Christian life these attributes as a cynosure are, that God we may revere plus imitate, plus solid consolation perceive.
